svg.title: Particle model overview
svg.desc: States & density: Solid: vibrate in fixed positions. Liquid: close, move past. Gas: far apart, random movement. ρ = m/V. Gas has low density from large spacing. Ice is less dense than liquid water. Density practical: Balance → mass. Regular solid: dimensions → volume. Irregular solid: displaced water → volume. Liquid: subtract empty-container mass. Read meniscus at eye level; avoid trapped bubbles. Temperature changes: Internal energy = total particle kinetic + potential energy. Temperature links to average kinetic energy. ΔE = mcΔθ. c: energy to warm 1 kg by 1°C, J/kg°C. State changes: Physical and reversible; mass conserved in a closed sample. E = mL. During melting/boiling, potential energy rises, temperature stays constant. Fusion: solid/liquid; vaporisation: liquid/gas. Pressure from collisions: Gas particles hit walls → force per area. Force is perpendicular to wall. At fixed volume and mass, warming → faster particles, more frequent/harder collisions → higher pressure. Compress a gas: Fixed mass, constant temperature: p₁V₁ = p₂V₂. Smaller volume → more wall collisions → greater p. Rapid compression does work on gas → internal energy and temperature can increase.
